title: Your own printf wrapper
description:
Write variadic functions with `stdarg.h`.

```
sum_ints(4, 1, 2, 3, 4) = 10
max_of(3, 7, 2, 9) = 9
log_line("WARN", "disk %d%% full", 91) -> [WARN] disk 91% full
```
hints: `va_list ap; va_start(ap, count); for (...) total += va_arg(ap, int); va_end(ap);` (lesson 7.01).
A function that forwards `...` needs the `v` version: `vprintf(fmt, ap)` takes a `va_list`.
requirements: `int sum_ints(int count, ...)` and `int max_of(int count, ...)` read `count` ints with `va_arg`.
`void log_line(const char *level, const char *fmt, ...)` passes its arguments to `vprintf`.
Mark `log_line` with `__attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)))` so the compiler checks its format strings (GCC and Clang).
stretch: Write `char *format_new(const char *fmt, ...)` that allocates exactly enough memory, using `vsnprintf` twice.
